land.text: Angeln, the Anglian homeland in southern Jutland

successors.note: Cliopatria's Scandinavian minor kingdoms shape of 500 covers five of the six Angeln cells; the pages do not name a successor. The page: 'The rest of that people stayed at the centre of the Angle homeland.'

land.text: the Anglian share of the English settlement

successors.note: 'During the fifth century, the Anglii invaded Great Britain' and founded Northumbria, East Anglia and Mercia (eu-11 writes those); the people, not the Angeln land.

capitals.name: Schleswig (Sleswic / Haithaby)
capitals.note: Æthelweard (died about 1000) 'equated the Anglian homeland with Schleswig and the Hedeby area' and gave the capital as 'Sleswic' in Old English and 'Haithaby' in Danish; the page dates no capital in the 4th-5th centuries, so this is a traditional seat.

keyframe_review.note: 1,293 km2 in Angeln (9.2-9.9 E, 54.5-54.9 N). The page: the Anglii lived 'probably in the southern part of the Jutland peninsula'; 'a small peninsular area is still called Angeln today', a triangle from Flensburg to Schleswig and Maasholm; finds from Schleswig date 'from the fourth and fifth centuries' (Borgstedt, Thorsberg, Nydam). Tacitus (about 98) places the Anglii beyond the Semnones and Langobardi near the Elbe, Ptolemy (about 150) inland between the Rhine and the Elbe (a placing 'Schütte judged ... mistaken'). The page gives no area; Angeln is the right size and place for the shape.
The same 1,293 km2 shape as 387-475; Cliopatria splits the row at 476 (where its Kingdom of Thuringia begins) without a change of land. The page records no event in 476. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: Angeln, 'a small peninsular area' on the Baltic coast of Schleswig-Holstein, a triangle from Flensburg to the city of Schleswig and on to Maasholm

ledger.note: 387: the Angles hold Angeln. The page gives no founding year; 387 is Cliopatria's first shape. Tacitus (about 98) is 'the earliest surviving mention'; finds from Schleswig date 'from the fourth and fifth centuries'.

The Angles cross to Britain in the 5th century. 'During the fifth century, the Anglii invaded Great Britain'; the page gives no year (441 is the start of Cliopatria's Anglo-Saxon England row); they founded the kingdoms of the Heptarchy (Northumbria, East Anglia, Mercia).

479: Angeln passes out of Anglian hands in Cliopatria's reading. Bede (died 735) says Angulus, the land between the Jutes and Saxons, 'remains unpopulated to this day', but 'The rest of that people stayed at the centre of the Angle homeland'; the page gives no date for any depopulation.

certainty.note: A tribal homeland known from Tacitus, Ptolemy and later tradition, with no border given by any source.

sources.title: Angles
sources.note: A disambiguation page: it only points to 'Angles (tribe)'; the redirect was followed.

sources.title: Angles (tribe)
sources.note: The homeland (Angeln, southern Jutland), Tacitus and Ptolemy, the 5th-century invasion of Britain, Bede on the empty Angulus, Æthelweard's capital.

notes: Cliopatria's Angles row (387-479, two shapes of 1,293 km2) is Angeln. The pages (2) give no founding or ending year: Tacitus about 98 is the earliest mention (Cliopatria's 387 begins three centuries later), 'during the fifth century' the invasion of Britain, Bede the empty Angulus. So found 387, split (to Anglo-Saxon England) 441 and dissolve 479 are confidence 1 and Cliopatria's own; a gap-filler could open Bede or 'Anglo-Saxon settlement of Britain'. The Anglian kingdoms in Britain (Northumbria, East Anglia, Mercia, Deira, Bernicia) belong to eu-11. The page 'Angles' is a disambiguation page to 'Angles (tribe)' (the wikipedia title in Cliopatria is 'Angles'). No wars in the pages. Family 'britain' follows the English kingdoms. Gazetteer: no 'Angeln' region; the dossier uses Cliopatria's own shape. Budget: two pages.
